caption: R1 800 of takeaways because cooking for one feels pointless. Is that just me?

slides.title:
How I spend my
R43 500 p/m
after my divorce
Living in Saldanha Bay
slides.body:
Male, 41
Divorced, two kids (12 and 9) with him every second weekend
Job: Plant supervisor, steel works
Net salary: R43 500 p/m

slides.title: Maintenance
slides.includes: Court-ordered for the two kids, by debit order on the 1st
slides.body: I don't resent it. I resent how much of it I used to spend without noticing.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 3 bed house so the kids each have a room
slides.body: It's too big for me during the week. It isn't too big on the weekends they're here.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.body: I kept the kids on mine. Their mother has her own.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: I bought it in the marriage. I'd have chosen differently on my own.

slides.title: Groceries & takeaways
slides.includes: Weekdays alone, weekends with the kids
slides.body: Takeaways are R1 800 of that. Cooking for one is the thing I still haven't got the hang of.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, electricity, phone, kids' activities, funeral policy, black tax, savings
slides.body: Black tax is R2 000 and nothing about the divorce changed it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R43 500. On paper I earn well. After the maintenance and the house I have about R1 300.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and it showed me the budget I was actually living, not the one I'd planned.

Takeaways were the line I didn't see coming.

No bank login needed.
